summary: Minimal, correct fix removing a stale `s.replace('.[', '[')` that corrupted parametrize ids/headlines (e.g. '..[' shown as '.['). Matches the actual upstream resolution; modern node-chain joining never emits '.[' as a separator, so the replace only ever damaged legitimate bracket content.

issues.description: Removing the replace assumes no current code path legitimately produces a '.[' that needs collapsing. In modern pytest getmodpath joins parts and the bracketed parametrize id is part of the node name, so '.[' as a join artifact no longer occurs; regression risk is low but the removed line's original intent is undocumented.

No comment added explaining why the historical `.replace('.[', '[')` was dropped; a one-line note would help future readers who hit the same 'I can't find this line's purpose' confusion the author mentioned.
